A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CoPA research. Their complete text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: V1 reports original detector-evasion experiments on three datasets, ablations, an adaptive-defense experiment, and automated and human text-quality evaluations.

after.justification: V3 retains these original empirical results and adds truncation, alternative-prompt, and linguistic-diversity measurements in its appendices.

M1.justification: The two prompted distributions, contrastive logit calculation in Equation 3, and adaptive truncation in Equation 4 remain unchanged. V3 tests prompt and truncation variants without replacing the proposed procedure or its default prompts.

E1.justification: New Appendix G adds an academic-style rewriting scenario through an explicit output-style instruction, evaluated on GPT-3.5-turbo-generated XSum texts. This is a limited scenario extension: the three English datasets and source-model coverage remain unchanged, and no academic corpus is added.

E2.justification: Dipper, Raidar-A, RedTeaming, and the eight target detectors remain in their corresponding comparisons. The removed Qwen2.5-7B column represents a CoPA paraphraser configuration, not a competing attack method.

E3.justification: V3 introduces TTR, MTLD, and Div_syn metrics, a control without truncation, and alternative human-prompt settings. Table 5 drops the Qwen2.5-7B configuration. The main sampling protocol, FPR thresholds, default hyperparameters, and human-evaluation design remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V3 adds focused analyses of truncation's contribution (Table 7), prompt-style sensitivity (Table 9), and lexical and syntactic diversity (Table 10). These extend the existing extensive supplementary analyses, while the paraphraser study loses its Qwen2.5-7B variant.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The existing practice of averaging human ratings, including the ten-annotator setup, is retained.

E6.justification: New Tables 7, 9, and 10 add supplementary results; for example, Table 7 reports Fast-DetectGPT TPR of 19.67% without truncation versus 17.00% with CoPA. Table 5 removes nine Qwen2.5-7B results. Matched retained benchmark, adaptive-defense, and text-quality scores are unchanged.

T1.justification: The KL-distance definition, propositions, Theorem 1, and Appendix A proofs are unchanged. V3's advice to check the theorem's assumption in each application does not revise its formal conditions or mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about training-free contrastive paraphrasing, theoretical support, detector evasion, and semantic preservation. The added analyses support existing claims rather than redefine the main contributions.

C2.justification: Section 3.3 newly cautions readers to verify the theoretical assumption for their setting. The limitations now acknowledge semantic drift and potentially necessary repeated generations. New appendix discussion interprets truncation benefits, prompt-style flexibility, and linguistic-diversity results.

D1.justification: V3 supplies a concrete code-access link where v1 only promised release. Appendix B expands prompt-selection documentation, including detector likelihood as a selection proxy, and Appendix G supplies two exact alternative prompts. Core implementation and hardware disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V3 adds citations to Fang et al. (2025), Guo et al. (2024b), Kong et al. (2025), and Wu et al. (2025) for decoding, linguistic diversity, and safety context. The related-work taxonomy and positioning against prior paraphrase attacks remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: V3 makes local wording and typo corrections, expands prompt explanations, adds acknowledgments and author contact details, and inserts Appendix G, moving text-quality evaluation to Appendix H. The main narrative and section organization are largely retained.

P2.justification: V3 adds three compact tables and two prompt boxes, removes one column from Table 5, and reflows appendix displays. V1 Tables 7 and 8 become v3 Tables 8 and 11. Existing figures are retained, and citations and cross-references become blue.

improvement.justification: The new truncation and linguistic-diversity analyses provide direct evidence for previously asserted component benefits and text properties. Prompt documentation, a code link, and clearer limitations also improve transparency. These limited gains outweigh the loss of Qwen2.5-7B results; the main benchmark evidence and theoretical framework remain unchanged.
